pr_body:
Fixes #30402

The problem was that `is_action` returns true for both `ui_left` and `ui_right` on horizontal axis input (and analogously with vertical). Not sure if this is intended, so my fix just works around that.
pr_comments: Would it be worth considering changing `is_action` itself so that manual input mapping from code to joystick would be fixed as well? i.e. If we map left stick Right to an input string, then we usually expect that left stick Left would not trigger it.

Yes, that was more or less intended. 
Sometimes, when you move the stick too fast, there was no event triggered telling you that the value should be set to zero if you quit one of the side. So to avoid problems, the events had to be kept for the other side of the stick.
This actually works fine in scripts, only C++ source seems to be affected.

issue_context.title: HSlider misbehaving with analog input
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version:**
3.1.1-stable


**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10

**Issue description:**
When mapping analog gamepad input to `ui_left` and `ui_right`, HSlider interprets all movements as "to the left". Other controls seem to respect it.

**Steps to reproduce:**
Run MRP, connect gamepad, move left stick to the right.


**Minimal reproduction project:**
https://github.com/lekoder/godot-issue-hslider-analog
comments: VSlider seems to have this problem too.
Couldn't reproduce on MAXJoypad emulator. It's working fine on it. I doubt this info was of any use.
Original report experienced using XBox360 physical controller.

review_comments:
Looks good, but you should likely register the default value into _bind_methods using DEFVAL. [At line 115.](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a33fc2a5994a5df711a8e2c881d6ac31b37a9fa6/core/os/input_event.cpp#L115)
This is necessary when generating the documentation.
Why not simply use p_event->is_action_pressed("ui_left") ? That would be cleaner :)
Ok, so the `is_pressed` part is unnecessary, but `is_action_pressed` won't trigger on echo events, so I need to use strength anyways.

Using strength here is kind of a dirty workaround, it's not supposed to be reliably used as whether or not something is pressed or not.
I'd rather add an optional argument to is_action_pressed for it to match echo events too if needed. That would be cleaner I think.
Ok, I added optional `p_allow_echo` to `is_action_pressed`. Will squash the commits when approved.
